popCulture.title: Description of Greece
popCulture.creator: Pausanias
popCulture.description: Pausanias makes Ogyges (Ogygus) first king of the Ectenes in the Theban land and links his name to the epithet Ogygian — and to a deluge remembered before Deucalion's.

popCulture.title: Ogyges
popCulture.description: Boeotian and Attic first king of the Ogygian flood — the deluge that drowned Copais and left Attica kingless until Cecrops in local memory.

popCulture.title: Ogygian deluge
popCulture.description: The earlier Greek flood named for Ogyges — set before Deucalion and Pyrrha in the layered flood chronologies of Boeotia and Attica.

popCulture.title: Thebes, Greece
popCulture.description: Poets call Thebes Ogygian from Ogyges — the primeval king's name fossilized in the city's oldest byname.
